structure: Part 9, Addresses and the address-book handshake. Read in full under src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/: page.js, evaluation.js, controller.js, template.njk, parties.js, frozen-parties.js, party-for-fulfilment-id.js, party-inline.js, assert-party-bindings.js, ins-handshake.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js; every file in party-picker/ (party-picker.controller.js and its test, party-picker.njk, _address-picker.njk and its test, request-params.js, selection.js and its test, view-model/index.js, address-lines.js, error-summary.js, pagination/index.js, page-numbers.js, results-href.js); every file in party-edit/ (party-edit.controller.js and its test, party-edit.njk, edit-href.js, address-rules.js and its test, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js); address-return/controller.js; fit/hub-picker.fit.spec.js, fit/party-edit.fit.spec.js, fit/axe.js; and src/server/app/services/address-book/ (client.js, index.js, to-wire-address.js, stub/index.js, stub/from-row.js). Supporting look-ups only: the addressHandshake, errorSummary and saveActions entries of shared/copy.en.js, CYA_SLUG in shared/kit.js, the party obligation ids in obligations/sections/parties.js, and the test names of addresses/controller.test.js and address-return/controller.test.js. Layout: one hub page (/addresses) with a summary-list row per party plus a conditional CPH row; one shared picker controller serving five party routes (<role>/select) over one untyped address book; one shared edit controller serving five party edit routes plus the contact edit route; an INS handshake that builds the 'Add a new address' link and a GET /address-return route that commits the returned address; and a read-only address-book client with a stub book. Claims run: hub (001-030), party copy (031-045), picker (046-090), party edit (091-132), handshake and return (133-152), address-book client and stub (153-172), fit tests and the axe helper (173-193), gaps (194-196). The CPH page itself and the contact picker are part 10's; only the hub's CPH row and the contact party's shared edit route are claimed here.

claims.statement: Party fulfilment ids exist only for single (scalar) party answers; an indexed or grouped party binding is refused.
Each add-address link carries a fresh random 16-byte handshake token, remembered in a cookie keyed by fulfilment id.

  storeHandshakeToken(request, h, fulfilmentId, token)

claims.statement: The INS address book returns the trader to the journey's address-return page, a GET route that reads fulfilment-id, addressId and handshake-token from the query.
claims.quote:
const fulfilmentId = request.query['fulfilment-id'] ?? ''
  const addressId = request.query.addressId ?? ''
  const handshakeToken = request.query['handshake-token'] ?? ''

claims.statement: A return with a fulfilment id that matches no party is rejected as a bad request ('Unknown fulfilment').
A return with no address id sends the trader to the party's picker without saving anything.
A return whose handshake token does not match the one remembered for that fulfilment id is rejected as a bad request ('Invalid handshake').
A verified handshake token is used once: it is cleared, and the cookie is removed when no tokens remain.
The returned address id is looked up in the signed-in organisation's own address book, so an id from another organisation is treated as not found.
If the address book cannot be reached on return, the trader goes to the picker with the 'unavailable' handshake error.
If the returned address is not found or is soft-deleted, the trader goes to the picker with the 'not-found' handshake error.
A good return stores a copy of the returned address as that party's answer, exactly as a picker selection would.
If saving the returned address fails, the trader goes to the picker with the 'unavailable' handshake error.

claims.statement: The frontend refuses to call the address book without an organisation from the signed-in session, rather than asking for an empty book.
Every address-book request carries the organisation in the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header, taken from the authenticated session and matching the path.

claims.statement: The address book runs no authentication of its own and trusts the organisation header, so organisation scoping of addresses depends entirely on the frontend sending the session's organisation.

/** The organisation is the authorisation — the address book runs no in-service
 * authentication and trusts this header (see its IdentityHeaderFilter). It must
 * always come from the authenticated session, never a payload or a stored
 * field, and it must match the orgId in the path (cv-010). */
